requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read refers to a terminology definition, the agent can
read its declaration with `read_node` using the definition's domain identity.
The SDK records each definition the agent reads.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` states no structural obligation, so no implementation root needs an {impl} reference.

I checked each clause for a required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named-interface delegation:

- **Complete declarations.** The clause is "every terminology definition ... MUST contribute its complete fenced declaration, including its phrase option". It describes what content reaches the mandatory input set. A different internal design could still supply the same declarations, for example by reading them from a cache, re-parsing the book, or building them in another module. The result would be the same, so how it is built is discretionary.
- **Transitive closure.** The clause is "referenced by those definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or nontermination on cycles". It states results: the set is closed, has no duplicates, and terminates. A recursive walk, an iterative worklist, or a precomputed closure would all satisfy it, so no algorithm is prescribed.
- **Reading a definition.** The clause is "the agent can read its declaration with `read_node` using the definition's domain identity. The SDK records each definition the agent reads." This describes what the tool does when called and that reads are recorded. It does not require a particular type, signature, or delegation. Any implementation that serves a `Definition` identity and records the read behaves the same.

The requirement's {cite} references to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and `requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` only supply context. `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` governs how the set is combined and supplied. `requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` governs the acknowledgment bodies. Neither adds a structural obligation to this subject. Behavioral evidence belongs to the test criterion, not this one.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.

**Subject-referenced definitions, transitive inclusion, no duplicates, cycles.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` has a requirement that cites `terms.unit` directly.
- In that test, `terms.unit` and `terms.value` reference each other, so they form a cycle.
- The test asserts that exactly two definition inputs are supplied. That checks that the transitively reached `terms.value` is included, that nothing is duplicated, and that preparation terminates on the cycle.

**Contributed-source references.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` puts a `{term}` reference to `terms.ready` in a contributed source file, `src/lib.rs`.
- It asserts that a definition input for `terms.ready` is supplied.

**Acknowledgment-referenced definitions, complete declaration, phrase option.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads]` references `terms.boundary` only from a fixme body.
- `terms.boundary` in turn references `terms.unit`, so the test exercises transitive inclusion.
- It asserts that each definition input's `text` equals the full fenced declaration line for line, including the `:phrase:` line.
- It asserts that the containing implementation body is not supplied.
- It checks that evidence validation detects a change to the transitive definition `terms.unit`.
- It checks that evidence validation detects a missing definition input.

**Agent reads of a definition and recording.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads]` has the agent call `read_node` with `{"data":{"Definition":"terms.unused"}}`.
- It asserts that the recorded inputs include a definition entry with the complete declaration text, including `:phrase: sometimes`.
- It also asserts that the tool response text contains the declaration.
- It runs for both a citation subject and an example subject.

The phrase option and full declaration are asserted in the acknowledgment and read tests. The same mechanism serves the other reference paths, so no separate gap is evident. Every test carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read refers to a terminology definition, the agent can
read its declaration with `read_node` using the definition's domain identity.
The SDK records each definition the agent reads.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
